rules.title: Proposed ban on algorithmic rental price-fixing software
rules.requirement: Santa Monica's City Council considered drafting an ordinance to ban landlords from using rent-pricing software, such as YieldStar and RealPage, that shares non-public rent and occupancy data. The proposal was not law when this article was written, so check whether the Council later adopted it.
rules.coverage_conditions: As proposed, would apply to landlords renting residential property in Santa Monica. No building limits are described.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Council agenda item (Councilmembers Torosis, Raskin, Hall), March 11, 2025 meeting
rules.quoted_span: The proposed ordinance would ban the use of software such as YieldStar and RealPage, "which allow landlords to share non-public, sensitive information about rental rates and occupancy.
rules.penalty: Proposal called for "enforceable penalties for noncompliance" (details not specified).

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: San Francisco bans landlords from using AI or algorithmic software to set rents.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals in San Francisco. No building limits are described in this article.
rules.citation: San Francisco ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software (citation not given in document)
rules.quoted_span: A few U.S. cities are cracking down on landlords who use the AI software to set rents after San Francisco became the first city to ban its use in July 2023.
rules.conflict_note: The article dates San Francisco's ban to July 2023. Other reporting places the San Francisco ordinance in 2024. The effective date is left null pending verification against the official ordinance.

rules.title: San Diego draft ordinance on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: San Diego was reported to be drafting an ordinance similar to San Francisco's ban on algorithmic rent-pricing software. It was not law at the time of this article.
rules.coverage_conditions: As drafted, would apply to residential rentals in San Diego. No details are given.
rules.citation: San Diego draft ordinance (December 2024; citation not given in document)
rules.quoted_span: San Diego -- where rents have increased 21 percent since 2020 -- was drafting a similar ordinance in December, according to CalMatters.

rules.title: 2024 California bill to ban pricing algorithms using competitors' nonpublic data
rules.requirement: A 2024 California bill to ban pricing algorithms based on nonpublic data from competing companies did not advance. It is not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied statewide. No details are given.
rules.citation: Unnamed 2024 California bill (bill number not given in document)
rules.quoted_span: State lawmakers, however, failed to advance legislation last year "that would have banned the use of any pricing algorithms based on nonpublic data provided by competing companies," CalMatters reported.

notes: Secondary news source dated March 7, 2025, describing a Santa Monica Council agenda item to direct drafting of an ordinance banning algorithmic rent-pricing software. The ordinance was to return for approval within 60 days. This article does not show whether it was adopted by 2026-10-01, so the record is marked pending; verify the outcome. San Francisco's ban is reported with a likely inaccurate date (July 2023), and no citation is given. San Diego's draft and the failed 2024 California bill are identified only via CalMatters, with no bill or ordinance number. The federal DOJ/FTC actions against RealPage are out of scope.
